name: Jantar Mantar, Sansad Marg and Jantar Mantar Road
notes: Protest days are shown as the civic use of the street (temporary banners and tents), not as an area label. The observatory instruments come from the landmark registry.

footpath.surface: grey paver with a yellow and black kerb stripe; red sandstone paths inside the garden; a wide tarmac edge with a taxi lay-by on Sansad Marg
footpath.notes: 3 m pavement at the garden railing, a 2 m tarmac edge on Sansad Marg

lamps.kind: single and double-arm steel poles on the footpath edge; black cast lanterns on stone pillars in the garden

kinds: red sandstone and brick wall about 1.5 to 2 m
green iron railing with spear tops about 2.5 m round the garden and the pavement
yellow police barricades on wheels about 1.1 m high

signs.boards: green direction boards on posts; a red nameplate at the garden gate

life.people: visitors and school groups at the observatory, guards at the gates, cab drivers waiting along the kerb; on protest days people gather at the railing for sit-ins and rallies with banners, tents and chairs

wear_notes: a little more at the protest pavement (banners, tarps, chairs)

road.condition: wide dual carriageway about 12 m per direction including a 2 m taxi lay-by, good grey asphalt, clear white lines, a low yellow and black divider about 0.4 m wide

evidence.buildings.mix: sheet jantar_mantar 'Buildings': government blocks (Akashvani Bhawan, post office, Reserve Bank towers) and hotel towers around the observatory, low sandstone and cream blocks of the old government quarter; the observatory comes from the registry. Shares are an estimate
evidence.buildings.floors: sheet jantar_mantar 'Buildings': 5 to 12 storeys; 'Street-level top-up': low red sandstone and cream blocks
evidence.buildings.colours: sheet jantar_mantar 'Buildings': cream and brown blocks, red sandstone walls
evidence.buildings.materials: sheet jantar_mantar 'Boundaries' (red sandstone and brick walls) and 'Buildings' (plaster)
evidence.footpath: sheet jantar_mantar 'Street-level top-up': Sansad Marg has a wide tarmac edge, taxi parking uses the edge; a paved strip with a yellow and black kerb near the gates; a pavement about 3 m wide outside the garden railing; red stone path inside
evidence.lamps: sheet jantar_mantar 'Street lamps' and 'Street-level top-up': black cast lanterns on stone pillars in the garden, single and double-arm poles about 9 m, 35 to 40 m apart
evidence.boundaries: sheet jantar_mantar 'Street-level top-up': red sandstone and brick walls 1.5 to 2 m, green iron railing with spear tops about 2.5 m, yellow police barricades on wheels about 1.1 m high
evidence.greenery: sheet jantar_mantar 'Trees and planting': old rain trees and neem forming a continuous canopy 15 to 20 m high; a formal garden with neat lawns, palms and flowering shrubs
evidence.props: sheet jantar_mantar 'Street-level top-up' (yellow police barricades on wheels, rows of white taxis in a lay-by along both kerbs) and 'Parking and vehicles'
evidence.signs: sheet jantar_mantar 'Edge blending' (shop signs vanish) and 'Street-level top-up' (green direction boards on posts, a red nameplate at the garden gate)
evidence.life: sheet jantar_mantar 'Vendors and street life' (tourists and school groups inside, guards at the gate, ice cream and tea carts, sit-ins at the roadside) and 'Street-level top-up' (taxi rows, guards, crowds with flags on protest days; the street is quiet outside protest days)
evidence.sound: sheet jantar_mantar 'What makes this area unlike the others': a green park beside a government road; 'Street-level top-up': quiet outside protest days
evidence.wear: sheet jantar_mantar 'Typical clutter and wear': wear 0.1; 'Street-level top-up': about 0.1 to 0.15 on the road; DELHI_WORLD.md 2a table 0.1 to 0.15
evidence.wear_notes: sheet jantar_mantar 'Street-level top-up': more at the protest site (banners, tarps, chairs)
evidence.road: sheet jantar_mantar 'Street-level top-up': about 12 m per direction (three lanes plus a parking edge), a continuous low yellow and black block about 0.4 m wide as the divider; 'Road surface and markings': good grey asphalt, slightly better kept than a typical arterial
